recognize_zh: 單顆細胞的核有深切口、形成雙葉相連的「蘋果核」形狀 (apple-core/bilobed nucleus)，細胞質少、帶細小紫紅顆粒，這種核形是急性前骨髓細胞白血病 (APL) 異常前骨髓細胞的線索。
features: Single medium-sized atypical cell, about twice the diameter of a red cell, with high N:C ratio
Nucleus with a deep central cleft producing a bilobed, apple-core/butterfly shape
Finely granular chromatin with a faint possible nucleolus
Thin rim of cytoplasm with fine purplish granules obscuring the nuclear border; no Auer rods seen
Background red cells show mild anisocytosis with occasional elongated forms; no platelets seen
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows an atypical mononuclear cell with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio and a deeply clefted, bilobed nucleus with an apple-core configuration. The chromatin is fine and the scant cytoplasm contains fine azurophilic granules that partly overlie the nucleus; Auer rods are not seen in this field. Platelets are not identified. Findings are suggestive of an abnormal promyelocyte of acute promyelocytic leukemia (hypogranular pattern) and warrant urgent coagulation assessment and PML::RARA testing.

ddx.vs: Promonocytes have gently folded nuclei with more abundant grey-blue cytoplasm and are nonspecific esterase positive with weak or absent MPO, unlike the strongly MPO-positive APL cell.
Reactive lymphocytes have abundant basophilic cytoplasm hugging red cells and lack a bilobed nucleus with azurophilic granules.
Normal promyelocytes have round to oval eccentric nuclei with a perinuclear hof and coarse primary granules, not a bilobed apple-core nucleus.
